title: The Fallback as Signal: Preserved Human Skill, Liability, and Competence Signaling in Credence-Good Markets under Improving AI
abstract: arXiv:2608.04276v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Firms that deploy improving but imperfect AI must decide how much to keep human workers engaged. Engagement lowers current output yet builds the fallback skill the firm needs when AI fails. We ask what that fallback skill signals to two audiences at once: mobile workers, who sort across firms on the skill trajectory a job builds, and clients, who cannot observe skill in a credence-good market and must infer competence. We embed the engagement-skill dynamics of Singh et al. (2026) in a signaling game and add a liability commitment. Because a more-skilled provider fails less often precisely in the states where AI is down, the expected cost of a liability pledge is decreasing in fallback skill. translated_title: 作为信号的备用能力：在AI改进下的信任品市场中，保留的人类技能、责任与能力信号传递
translated_abstract: 部署改进但不完美AI的企业必须决定让人类工人保持多大程度的参与。参与度降低当前产出，但会积累企业在AI失效时所需的备用技能。我们探讨这种备用技能如何同时向两类受众传递信号：一是流动工人，他们会根据工作所构建的技能轨迹在企业间进行选择；二是客户，他们在信任品市场中无法直接观察技能，必须推断企业的能力。我们将Singh等人（2026）的参与-技能动态嵌入到一个信号传递博弈中，并加入责任承诺机制。由于技能更高的提供者在AI失效的状态下恰恰更少出错，因此责任承诺的预期成本随备用技能的提高而递减。这在一个内生的（即构建而非天赋的）类型上恢复了Spence-Mirrlees单交叉条件，并产生了一个分离均衡，在该均衡中，责任承诺证明了保留的人类能力——这种能力是任何人工制品在AI写作能力达到同等水平后都无法证明的。
tldr: 本文提出在AI改进的信任品市场中，责任承诺可以作为传递人类备用技能的信号机制，在技能内生积累的条件下实现分离均衡，从而证明人类能力在AI失效时的独特价值。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes that liability commitment can serve as a signaling mechanism for preserved human fallback skills in credence-good markets under improving AI, achieving a separating equilibrium with endogenous skill accumulation and certifying human competence that artifacts cannot replicate.
